entities.summary: The Royal Danish Army is the land-based branch of the Danish Armed Forces, together with the Danish Home Guard. For the last decade, the Royal Danish Army has undergone a massive transformation of structures, equipment and training methods, abandoning its traditional role of anti-invasion defence, and instead focusing on out of area operations by, among other initiatives, reducing the size of the conscripted and reserve components and increasing the active component, changing from 60% support structure and 40% operational capability, to 60% combat operational capability and 40% support structure.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Royal Danish Army's transformation has led to a significant reduction in its conscripted and reserve components, from 60% support structure and 40% operational capability to 60% combat operational capability and 40% support structure. This shift has allowed the army to focus on out-of-area operations and increase its active component.
